params.body:
The Status column on the schools list said "in gebruik" nine times out of nine.
It read `schools.active`, and that flag has stood on 1 for every school ever
created; nobody turns it off. Measured on production tonight:

| school | `active` | last school year with an offering |
| --- | --- | --- |
| athena Heule | 1 | 2026-2027 |
| CLW | 1 | 2026-2027 |
| athena OV4 | 1 | 2026-2027 |
| athena Drie Hofsteden | 1 | 2026-2027 |
| athena Pottelberg Kortrijk | 1 | 2023-2024 |
| ZOOM Kortrijk | 1 | 2023-2024 |
| Futura | 1 | 2022-2023 |
| MSKA Roeselare | 1 | 2022-2023 |
| Atheneum Bellevue Izegem | 1 | 2022-2023 |

Five of nine stopped years ago. A column that always gives the same answer is
not a column.

## What changed

The flag stays, because the code acts on it: a school with `active = false`
stops getting reports (`SchoolNoLongerReportsException`). What it does not do is
answer "is this school using Naviskore", so the screen no longer claims it does.
Next to it, measured:

- teaching in the current school year, and on → **in gebruik**
- on, but its newest offering is older → **aan, laatst lesaanbod in 2023-2024**
- on, and never any offering → **aan, nog geen lesaanbod**
- off → **staat uit**, unchanged

`App\Services\SchoolManagement\SchoolActivity` does the measuring, in two cheap
queries for the whole list rather than one per row. It is deliberately not a
scope on `School` and deliberately not written back to the row: a derived answer
that gets stored goes stale exactly the way `active` did. It orders on
`start_date` and not on the id, because the ids happen to run in order today and
a year added out of order later would break a comparison on them silently.

## One bug found while testing it

`Schoolyear::current()` throws `SchoolyearCurrentDoesNotExistException` when
nobody has created the current year yet, and adding it to the list's render made
the whole screen a 500. A list of schools is not where that should surface, so
it is caught: with no current year no school can be teaching in it, and every row
reads as the year it last taught. `SchoolControllerTest > it lists the schools`
caught this, and there is now a test of its own for it.

## What this does not do

It does not switch the five idle schools off. That decision is yours: a school
that is off stops getting reports, and five rows of production data are not
something a pull request should change on its own. The screen now shows you
which five they are.

## Checks

- `php artisan test`: 196 passed, 1 failed (`BuildStampTest`, which needs a full
  clone rather than a worktree). Nine new assertions across two new test classes.
- `vendor/bin/phpstan analyse`: no errors. `vendor/bin/pint --test`: passed.
params.title: De schoollijst zegt wat ze meet
